KN.investment_route: Donation to the SISC fund (250000 USD for main applicant or family of up to 4); Developer's real estate investment (325000 USD fractional ownership, or 600000 USD for full ownership, in an approved development, 7yr resale restriction); Approved public benefit project
KN.investment_breakdown: SISC: main applicant or family of up to 4 members at USD 250,000; each additional dependant under 18 adds USD 25,000; each additional dependant 18 or over adds USD 50,000; funds five priorities: local food production, green energy transition, economic diversification, sustainable industry, and social protection. Real estate: minimum USD 325,000 per main applicant for fractional ownership in an approved development, or from USD 600,000 for full ownership; resaleable after 7 years
KN.additional_fees: SISC route: due diligence fee of USD 10,000 for the main applicant plus USD 7,500 per dependant aged 16 or over. Real estate route: same due diligence fees, plus post-approval application fees of USD 25,000 (main applicant), USD 15,000 (spouse), USD 10,000 (dependant under 18), USD 15,000 (dependant 18+), plus compulsory insurance fund contributions and conveyance fees
KN.physical_presence_requirement: none required to obtain or maintain citizenship
KN.due_diligence: interview is mandatory for the main applicant, conducted virtually or in person by an independent firm commissioned by the CIU or by CIU officials; dependants aged 16 or over may also be required to attend an interview if deemed necessary; applications from citizens of Afghanistan, Belarus, Iran, Iraq, North Korea, and Russia are not accepted; biometric enrolment introduced 2026
KN.family_inclusion: Spouse; children under 18; children aged 18-30 in full-time secondary or tertiary education and fully supported by the main applicant; children 18+ who are physically or mentally challenged; parents of the main applicant or spouse aged 55+ living with and fully supported by the main applicant
KN.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period, physical presence, or naturalization wait is required
KN.renewal_requirements: citizenship is granted for life; no residency requirement to maintain it; the passport itself is renewed periodically like any other passport
KN.eligibility_criteria: Main applicant must be 18+; must make or agree to make the legally prescribed investment; must pass due diligence checks and financial criteria; not eligible if previously denied citizenship of any country, denied a visa to a country St Kitts and Nevis citizens can enter visa-free (and not since obtained that visa), has a criminal record, is under criminal investigation, was declared bankrupt within the preceding 10 years, or is involved in activity likely to cause disrepute to St Kitts and Nevis
KN.key_benefits: Visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 150+ destinations including the UK, Schengen Area, Hong Kong, and Singapore; No personal income, capital gains, wealth, or inheritance tax; Oldest continuously running CBI program in the world, established 1984
KN.taxation_notes: no tax on worldwide income, capital gains, gifts, or inheritance for citizens who are not otherwise tax-resident elsewhere
KN.application_steps: Select an Authorised Agent (applications cannot be submitted directly to the CIU); complete all forms and supply required documents through the Authorised Agent; attend an interview if required; the CIU processes the application and conducts due diligence, advising within 120-180 days whether it is approved-in-principle, denied, or delayed for cause; make the SISC contribution or complete the real estate purchase; receive the certificate of naturalisation and apply for a St Kitts and Nevis passport
KN.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — no requirement to renounce any prior nationality

AG.investment_route: Donation to the National Development Fund (NDF), minimum USD 230,000; Real estate investment of at least USD 300,000 into an approved project, held at least 5 years; Business investment of at least USD 1,500,000 as a sole investor, or a joint investment totaling at least USD 5,000,000 with each of at least 2 investors contributing at least USD 400,000; Contribution of USD 260,000 (inclusive of processing fees) to the University of the West Indies Five Islands Campus Fund
AG.investment_breakdown: NDF and Real Estate routes: processing fee USD 10,000 for a single applicant or USD 20,000 for a family of up to 4, plus USD 10,000 for each additional dependant beyond 4; Business route: same processing fee structure; UWI Fund route: the USD 260,000 contribution already includes processing fees, with USD 10,000 added per additional dependant
AG.additional_fees: due diligence fee of USD 8,500 for the principal applicant, plus USD 5,000 for a spouse, USD 2,000 per dependant aged 12-17, and USD 4,000 per dependant aged 18-30 or per dependent parent/grandparent aged 55+ (business route due diligence for spouse is USD 75,000 for the single-investor tier); USD 5,000 benefactor fee; passport fee of USD 300 per person
AG.processing_time: typically within 3-4 months from a complete application
AG.physical_presence_requirement: none required to obtain citizenship, but citizenship may be revoked if the citizen does not spend at least 5 days in Antigua and Barbuda within the first 5 calendar years after being granted citizenship
AG.due_diligence: rigorous background checks on all applicants; disqualifying factors include false information on the application, a family member with a contagious disease or serious health problem, a prior conviction with a maximum penalty over 6 months imprisonment without a free pardon, being the subject of a criminal investigation, being a national security risk, activity likely to cause disrepute to Antigua and Barbuda, or having been denied a visa to a visa-free-travel country and not since obtained that visa
AG.family_inclusion: Spouse of the main applicant; child of the main applicant or spouse aged 0-30 who is financially dependent; child 18+ who is physically or mentally challenged, living with and fully supported by the main applicant; parent or grandparent of the main applicant or spouse aged 55+ who is financially dependent; unmarried sibling of the main applicant or spouse; future spouse of the main applicant (USD 50,000 fee payable on application); future spouse of a dependent child, provided that dependant is under 35 at the time of application; future child of a dependent child (USD 10,000 for a child under 6, USD 25,000 for a child aged 6-17)
AG.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval; the 5-day stay requirement is the only presence obligation and can be fulfilled any time within 5 years
AG.renewal_requirements: citizenship is permanent; no renewal beyond standard passport reissuance
AG.eligibility_criteria: 18+ for the main applicant; must select one of the four investment routes; must pass due diligence; disqualified by false information on the application, a disqualifying criminal record, an active criminal investigation, being deemed a national security risk, activity likely to cause disrepute to Antigua and Barbuda, or a relevant unresolved prior visa refusal
AG.key_benefits: Visa-free access to 150+ destinations including the UK, Schengen Area, and Hong Kong; One of the lower-cost options for a family of four; 5-day stay requirement is uniquely light compared to peer programs; note: a US Presidential Proclamation (10998, effective 1 January 2026) partially restricts US visas for Antiguan nationals — holders of valid US visas issued before that date are unaffected, but prospective travelers should check current US entry requirements
AG.taxation_notes: no tax on worldwide income, capital gains, or inheritance
AG.application_steps: engage a licensed agent (direct applications to the CIU are not accepted); complete the prescribed application forms and gather supporting documents including police certificates; the agent submits the application and pays the 10% non-refundable government fee deposit; the CIU conducts due diligence; on approval, pay the balance of the government fee, complete the chosen investment, and pay due diligence and passport fees; receive the certificate of registration and passport
AG.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — no requirement to renounce any prior nationality

DM.investment_route: Donation to the Economic Diversification Fund (EDF), minimum USD 200,000; Purchase of a unit in a government-approved real estate project, minimum USD 200,000, held 3 years from the date citizenship is granted (5 years if the future buyer is also a CBI applicant)
DM.investment_breakdown: EDF: USD 200,000 for the main applicant, USD 250,000 for the main applicant plus up to 3 qualifying dependants, USD 25,000 for each additional dependant under 18, USD 40,000 for each additional dependant 18+. Real estate: the USD 200,000 property purchase itself, plus separate government fees of USD 75,000 (main applicant), USD 100,000 (main applicant plus up to 3 dependants), USD 25,000 per additional dependant under 18, USD 40,000 per additional dependant 18+ — these government fees apply only to the real estate route, not the EDF route
DM.additional_fees: processing fee USD 1,000 per application; due diligence fee USD 7,500 for the main applicant and USD 4,000 per dependant aged 16+; certificate of naturalisation fee USD 500 per person; mandatory interview fee USD 1,000 per person aged 16+; enhanced due diligence fees may apply depending on citizenship/nationality; applications from Belarus, Iran, Northern Iraq, North Korea, Russia, Yemen, and Sudan face bans, limits, or enhanced due diligence
DM.processing_time: typically a few months from a complete application to approval-in-principle
DM.physical_presence_requirement: none required to obtain or maintain citizenship
DM.due_diligence: multi-tiered due diligence process; mandatory interview for all applicants aged 16 and over; enhanced due diligence applies depending on nationality and personal circumstances; applications from Belarus, Iran, Northern Iraq, North Korea, Russia, Yemen, and Sudan face bans, limits, or enhanced scrutiny
DM.family_inclusion: Spouse; children (dependants relying on the main applicant as primary income source); parents; grandparents — eligibility for additional dependants scales the required contribution (USD 25,000 under 18, USD 40,000 if 18+)
DM.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period is required
DM.renewal_requirements: citizenship is permanent; passport renewed every 10 years
DM.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds; Medical exam
DM.key_benefits: The lowest headline cost among Caribbean CBI programs; Visa-free access to 140+ destinations including the UK, Schengen Area, Hong Kong, and Singapore; note: a US Presidential Proclamation (10998, effective 1 January 2026) partially restricts US visas for Dominican nationals — holders of valid US visas issued before that date are unaffected, but prospective travelers should check current US entry requirements
DM.taxation_notes: no tax on worldwide income, capital gains, or inheritance
DM.application_steps: select an Authorised Agent or promoter; pay due diligence fees and the agent submits the application; the application undergoes a multi-tiered due diligence process; if approved in principle, make the EDF contribution or complete the real estate Sale and Purchase Agreement and pay government fees; receive the certificate of naturalisation and apply for a Dominican passport
DM.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — officially confirmed by the CBIU: applicants may hold multiple citizenships alongside Dominican citizenship

GD.investment_route: Donation to the National Transformation Fund (NTF), minimum USD 235,000 for an individual, a couple, or a family of up to 4; Real estate investment in an approved project, from USD 270,000 (some approved projects require up to USD 350,000), plus a separate government contribution of USD 50,000; Significant Investment: purchase of a registered business or company operating in Grenada, or shares in a company or consortium
GD.investment_breakdown: NTF: flat USD 235,000 covers an individual, a couple, or a family of up to 4 (excluding siblings, and parents/grandparents 55 or under); beyond the third dependant, each additional dependant adds USD 25,000-50,000, and an additional sibling adds USD 75,000. Real estate: purchase price from USD 270,000-350,000 depending on the approved project, plus a mandatory USD 50,000 government contribution per application (family of up to 4), which does not apply to siblings/parents/grandparents 55 or under added to the application
GD.additional_fees: application fee USD 1,500 per person; due diligence fee USD 5,000 per adult (dependent children 0-16 pay nil, 17+ pay USD 5,000); processing fee USD 1,500 per person 17+ or USD 500 under 17; interview fee USD 1,000 per person 17+ including non-applicant spouse and sponsor
GD.processing_time: application approved within 60 business days of submission, subject to satisfactory due diligence and funds received
GD.physical_presence_requirement: none required to obtain citizenship — no need to visit Grenada before, during, or after the application process
GD.due_diligence: mandatory online interview for all applicants; thorough government background check; disqualifying factors include false information on the application, a prior conviction with a maximum penalty over 6 months without a free pardon, an active criminal investigation, being deemed a national security risk, activity likely to cause disrepute to Grenada, or an unresolved denial of a visa to a visa-free-travel country
GD.family_inclusion: Spouse (opposite sex, no criminal record); children under 18; children 18-30 who are fully financially dependent and apply together with the main applicant; parents and grandparents fully financially dependent on the main applicant or spouse; unmarried siblings over 18 with no children
GD.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period is required
GD.renewal_requirements: citizenship is for life; Grenadian passports are valid for 5 years and renewable by law without discretionary denial
GD.eligibility_criteria: 18+ for the main applicant, in good health, with legally-sourced funds sufficient for the chosen investment; no eligibility for those who provide false information, have a disqualifying criminal record, are under criminal investigation, are deemed a national security risk, are involved in activity likely to cause disrepute to Grenada, or have an unresolved visa refusal from a visa-free country
GD.key_benefits: The only Caribbean CBI program that gives access to the US E-2 Treaty Investor Visa (after roughly 3 years of citizenship, via Grenada's treaty with the US) without requiring US residency first; Visa-free access to 140+ destinations including China, the UK, and the Schengen Area
GD.taxation_notes: no tax on worldwide income, capital gains, or inheritance
GD.application_steps: choose an Authorised International Marketing Agent, who liaises with an Authorised Local Agent (direct applications to the CBIC are not accepted); complete official forms, attend a medical examination, and gather supporting documents, all legalised and translated into English; the Authorised Local Agent submits the application to the CBIC; attend the mandatory interview; the CBIC conducts due diligence and makes a recommendation, with final approval by the Minister of Citizenship; on approval, make the NTF contribution or complete the real estate purchase; receive the certificate of registration and apply for a passport
GD.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — officially confirmed by the IMA: applicants are not required to renounce any other citizenship or passport

LC.investment_route: National Economic Fund (NEF) donation, USD 240,000 covering the applicant plus up to 3 dependants; National Action Bond (NAB), non-interest-bearing, USD 300,000 for any number of dependants, held 5 years, plus USD 50,000 admin fee; Real estate purchase in an approved project, USD 300,000 plus administrative fees; Enterprise investment: USD 3,500,000 solo, or USD 6,000,000 joint venture with each investor contributing at least USD 1,000,000 (both plus USD 50,000 admin fee), or a lower Option 3 enterprise route at USD 250,000 covering the applicant plus up to 3 dependants
LC.investment_breakdown: NEF: USD 240,000 covers applicant + up to 3 dependants; each additional dependant under 18 adds USD 10,000, each 18+ adds USD 20,000; a spouse added later by an existing citizen costs USD 35,000, other dependants added later cost USD 25,000, a newborn under 12 months costs USD 5,000. Real estate admin fees: USD 30,000 applying alone, USD 45,000 with spouse, USD 5,000 per dependant under 18, USD 10,000 per dependant 18+, USD 10,000 each for dependants beyond 4. Enterprise Option 3 admin fees: USD 15,000 alone, USD 20,000 with spouse, USD 25,000 with 2 dependants, USD 30,000 with 3 dependants, USD 10,000 each additional dependant beyond 3
LC.additional_fees: application processing fee USD 2,000 for the main applicant plus USD 1,000 per dependant; due diligence fee USD 8,000 for the main applicant plus USD 5,000 per dependant (due diligence applies only to applicants over 16); mandatory interview and identity verification fee, payable by the main applicant only, in effect since September 2023
LC.processing_time: typically 60-90 days to a letter of approval; investment must be completed within 90 days of approval
LC.physical_presence_requirement: none required to obtain or maintain citizenship
LC.due_diligence: due diligence conducted on all applicants over 16; mandatory interview and identity verification for the main applicant only, in effect for all applications processed since 4 September 2023; the CIP Board holds the right to grant, deny, or delay any application for cause
LC.family_inclusion: Spouse; dependent children; a newborn child of a citizen 12 months or under can be added later for USD 5,000; a spouse can be added to existing citizenship later for USD 35,000; other qualifying dependants can be added later for USD 25,000
LC.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period is required
LC.renewal_requirements: citizenship is for life; real estate and bond investments must be held for 5 years before resale
LC.eligibility_criteria: 18+ for the main applicant; verifiable lawful source of funds; must select one of the five qualifying investment routes; subject to CIP Board discretion to grant, deny, or delay any application for cause
LC.key_benefits: The widest choice of investment routes among Caribbean CBI programs, including an interest-free government bond that returns full principal; Visa-free access to 140+ destinations
LC.taxation_notes: no tax on worldwide income, capital gains, or inheritance
LC.application_steps: select a licensed agent; choose one of the five investment routes and gather supporting documents; submit the application along with processing and due diligence fees; the main applicant completes the mandatory interview and identity verification process; on approval, complete the chosen investment within 90 days; receive the certificate of registration and passport
LC.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — no requirement to renounce any prior nationality

TR.investment_route: Real estate purchase worth at least USD 400,000, with a 3-year title-deed resale restriction, attested by the Ministry of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change; Fixed capital investment of at least USD 500,000, attested by the Ministry of Industry and Technology; Bank deposit of at least USD 500,000 held for 3 years, attested by the Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency; Government bonds worth at least USD 500,000 held for 3 years, attested by the Ministry of Treasury and Finance; Real estate investment fund or venture capital investment fund shares worth at least USD 500,000 held for 3 years, attested by the Capital Markets Board of Turkiye; Private pension system contribution of at least USD 500,000 held for 3 years, attested by the Insurance and Private Pension Regulation and Supervision Agency; Job creation for at least 50 people, attested by the Ministry of Labor and Social Security
TR.investment_breakdown: all thresholds are per Presidential decision published in the Official Gazette (18 September 2018 regulation, real estate raised from USD 250,000 to USD 400,000 in 2022); multiple smaller real estate purchases can be combined to reach USD 400,000; payments must be made in Turkish lira equivalent to the USD amount through the Turkish banking system; the real estate title deed and acquisition application must explicitly state the citizenship purpose and include a declaration not to sell for 3 years
TR.additional_fees: title deed transfer tax (generally 4%), notary and translation fees, and mandatory earthquake insurance for buildings; annual property tax and maintenance fees apply after purchase; government fees apply to the non-real-estate investment routes as well
TR.physical_presence_requirement: no residence permit is required as a pre-condition to acquire real estate in Turkiye, but successful applicants must visit Turkiye in person to submit biometrics for the residence application
TR.due_diligence: the relevant government body for each route (Ministry of Environment/Urbanization for real estate, Ministry of Industry and Technology for fixed capital, Banking Regulation and Supervision Agency for deposits, Ministry of Treasury and Finance for bonds, Capital Markets Board for fund shares, Insurance and Private Pension Regulation and Supervision Agency for pension contributions, Ministry of Labor and Social Security for job creation) must formally attest the investment before citizenship can be granted; final decision rests with the President of the Republic of Turkiye
TR.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted directly by Presidential resolution upon attestation of the qualifying investment — no residency period is required
TR.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Investment value must be maintained/held for the required period
TR.key_benefits: One of the fastest large-economy citizenship options; Qualifying US investors may separately pursue the E-2 Treaty Investor Visa; Visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 110+ destinations
TR.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed only if tax-resident in Turkey (183+ days per year); non-resident citizens owe no Turkish tax on foreign-sourced income
TR.application_steps: select a qualifying investment (commonly real estate); obtain an official appraisal report confirming value; complete purchase/deposit and register with authorities; apply for a conformity certificate; submit citizenship application and biometrics
TR.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Turkey allows dual and multiple citizenship

VU.investment_route: Donation to the Vanuatu Development Support Program (DSP), the primary and lowest-cost route, granting honorary citizenship; three other statutory routes also exist and are administered separately: the Capital Investment Immigration Plan (CIIP, Form D, substantially costlier), the Vanuatu Contribution Program (VCP), and the Real Estate Option (REO, requiring investment in a Vanuatu Government Approved Project since July 2021)
VU.investment_breakdown: DSP citizenship fee: USD 130,000 single applicant, USD 150,000 married couple, USD 165,000 married couple plus 1 child, USD 180,000 married couple plus 2 children, USD 10,000 per additional applicant; a mandatory USD 5,000 FIU due diligence fee applies per application. CIIP (Form D) is a separate, costlier route: citizenship fee USD 260,000 covers only the applicant, spouse, and 1 child under 18; each additional child under 18 costs USD 19,250, each dependant aged 18-21 costs USD 44,250
VU.additional_fees: application fee 5,000 Vatu per application (for all forms except Form D, which has a USD 250 application fee); USD 5,000 mandatory FIU due diligence fee for DSP applications; only US Dollar payments are accepted — the Citizenship Commission does not recognize or accept Bitcoin or any cryptocurrency for the DSP, CIIP, or REO programs
VU.due_diligence: mandatory FIU (Financial Intelligence Unit) due diligence review; the oath of allegiance for the applicant and spouse must be taken in the physical presence of a Commissioner for Oaths; the Citizenship Commission has revoked approximately 30 citizenships previously granted contrary to the Citizenship Act, and has stated it is enhancing due diligence and investment verification standards
VU.family_inclusion: spouse; children under 25 years; parents aged 50 and over
VU.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period
VU.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
VU.key_benefits: The fastest CBI program in the world, often completing in 30-60 days; No personal income, capital gains, or inheritance tax; Visa-free access to 90+ destinations
VU.taxation_notes: no personal income tax, capital gains tax, or inheritance tax of any kind
VU.application_steps: engage a licensed agent; submit documents and application forms; due diligence review by the Vanuatu Citizenship Office; pay the contribution; receive the certificate and passport
VU.status: active, under periodic EU visa-suspension scrutiny
VU.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — no requirement to renounce any prior nationality

EG.investment_route: Non-refundable donation of USD 250,000 to the state treasury; Real estate investment of USD 300,000 in state-approved property (reduced from USD 500,000 by a 2023 Prime Ministerial decree), held 5 years; Business investment of USD 350,000 in a new or existing local business plus a separate non-refundable USD 100,000 donation to the treasury, maintained 5 years; Bank deposit of USD 500,000, refundable in Egyptian pounds without interest after 3 years
EG.investment_breakdown: figures per Law No. 190 of 2019 and Prime Ministerial Decree No. 876 of 2023; October 2024 amendments permit joint real estate investments provided each participant's share exceeds USD 300,000, require private-developer purchases to go through an Egyptian bank account, and mandate building-permit verification for all properties in an application
EG.additional_fees: mandatory administrative fee of USD 10,000, transferred from abroad to the Central Bank of Egypt, applies to all routes
EG.processing_time: 3-6 months from application to Prime Ministerial decree
EG.physical_presence_requirement: no specific residency period is required, unlike programs such as Cyprus or Spain; approved applicants are granted temporary residence for 6 months in which to execute the chosen investment
EG.due_diligence: applications are reviewed by the Citizenship Application Examination Unit, affiliated with the Prime Minister's Office, with security clearance by the relevant national security authorities before approval
EG.family_inclusion: spouse; minor children up to age 21
EG.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted directly by decision of the Prime Minister once the investment is confirmed — no separate residency wait
EG.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
EG.key_benefits: Only North African sovereign CBI program; Provides a foothold for regional trade and business under Egypt's various trade agreements
EG.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed only if tax-resident in Egypt; non-resident citizens are taxed on Egyptian-source income only
EG.application_steps: submit application with supporting documents through official channels; complete the chosen investment; undergo Ministry of Interior security clearance; receive citizenship decree
EG.dual_citizenship: Permitted for most applicants, though certain senior public-office and security-sensitive roles are restricted to those holding only Egyptian citizenship

JO.investment_route: Purchase of newly issued shares in Jordanian companies through a licensed broker, minimum JOD 1,000,000, held at least 3 years with no more than 20% concentrated in a single company; New productive project in Amman Governorate, minimum JOD 700,000 in fixed/non-current assets averaged over 3 audited years, creating at least 20 Jordanian jobs (90% monthly compliance); New productive project outside Amman, minimum JOD 500,000, creating at least 10 Jordanian jobs (90% monthly compliance); Small/medium enterprise investment of USD 750,000, held at least 3 years; Larger company investment of JOD 3,000,000
JO.investment_breakdown: the program (launched 2018 under Jordan's investor citizenship framework) was formally revamped in July 2026: the Ministry of Investment raised the investment requirement for the Amman Stock Exchange share route and introduced stronger incentives to direct investment toward governorates and priority national sectors, explicitly measuring program success by economic impact (jobs, productive investment) rather than headcount of citizenships granted; the previous passive bank-deposit and government-bond routes (last set at USD 1,000,000 and USD 1,000,000 respectively under a 2019 Cabinet decision) have since been phased out in favor of these active, job-creating routes
JO.additional_fees: administrative processing fees apply in addition to the core investment; Cabinet approval carries no separate formal fee beyond standard filing costs
JO.processing_time: several months, subject to Cabinet-level and royal approval
JO.due_diligence: applications reviewed by a special investor committee, which submits its recommendation to the Minister of Interior; job-creation routes require Social Security Corporation registration and monthly compliance verification over the full holding period; for the project routes, a temporary passport is issued during the 3-year holding period, with full citizenship granted only after the holding period is completed
JO.naturalization_timeline: for the project-investment routes, a temporary passport is issued while the 3-year job-creation and holding requirements are being met; full citizenship is granted once the holding period concludes and compliance is confirmed; the share-purchase route can lead to citizenship more directly once the 3-year share-retention period and compliance checks are satisfied
JO.renewal_requirements: citizenship is permanent, though naturalised citizens are barred from holding senior public office for 10 years
JO.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
JO.key_benefits: access to Jordan's business environment at the crossroads of the Levant and Gulf, and to free-trade arrangements including Qualifying Industrial Zone access to US markets
JO.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed only if tax-resident in Jordan
JO.application_steps: apply through the Jordan Investment Commission; select the deposit or enterprise route; complete financial and security due diligence; obtain Cabinet approval and Royal Decree; receive citizenship
JO.dual_citizenship: Generally permitted in practice under the 1954 Nationality Law as amended in 1987, and dual nationals are not automatically stripped of Jordanian citizenship; citizens are formally required to notify the government of any foreign nationality held, and acquisition of the nationality of a non-Arab state can in some circumstances require Cabinet consent — investors should seek case-specific legal advice

NR.program_name: Naoero Economic and Climate Resilience Citizenship Program (ECRCP)
NR.investment_route: Non-refundable contribution to the Naoero Treasury Fund
NR.investment_breakdown: USD 90,000 for a Principal Applicant under a limited-time discount running until 31 December 2026 (standard rate USD 115,000 outside the promotional window); USD 2,000 per additional dependant aged 16+; USD 15,000 per sibling of the Principal Applicant or spouse
NR.additional_fees: application fee USD 5,000 (Principal Applicant) plus USD 2,000 per dependant; due diligence fee USD 6,000 (Principal Applicant) plus USD 3,000 per dependant 16+ or per benefactor; bank due diligence and transaction charge USD 1,200-2,200 depending on family size; passport fee USD 500 per passport
NR.processing_time: 3-4 months from submission to citizenship approval
NR.physical_presence_requirement: none required; the application process can be completed without traveling to Naoero, though a visit may be needed for the Oath of Allegiance unless taken remotely by audio-visual link or before a notary public
NR.due_diligence: mandatory interview for the Principal Applicant, conducted by an approved due diligence firm, virtually or in person; dependants aged 16+ may also be required to attend if deemed necessary; police clearance certificates required from every country of residence for 6+ months over the last 10 years
NR.family_inclusion: spouse; dependent children; parents; siblings — dependant age caps have been removed for children and parents
NR.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period
NR.renewal_requirements: Naoero passports are valid for 10 years for all applicants and are renewable without requiring a Naoero address
NR.eligibility_criteria: 18+ for the Principal Applicant; of good character with no criminal record; able to pass due diligence checks
NR.key_benefits: visa-free or visa-on-arrival access to 85+ destinations including Hong Kong, Singapore, and the UAE; unrestricted dual citizenship; contributions fund Naoero's climate resilience and Higher Ground Initiative infrastructure projects
NR.taxation_notes: no personal income tax, capital gains tax, or inheritance tax
NR.application_steps: select a licensed Agent (direct applications to the Program Office are not accepted); prepare documents including police clearance certificates; undergo due diligence review and the mandatory interview; make the Treasury Fund contribution and pay associated fees; take the Oath of Allegiance (in person, by audio-visual link, or before a notary); receive the certificate of citizenship and passport
NR.dual_citizenship: Permitted — no requirement to renounce any prior nationality

ST.investment_route: Non-refundable donation to the National Transformation Fund (NTF)
ST.investment_breakdown: USD 90,000 for a single applicant; USD 95,000 for a couple or family of up to 4; USD 5,000 for each additional dependant from the 5th onward; funds are directed to renewable energy, infrastructure, education, affordable housing, and eco-tourism projects; legal basis is Decree-Law No. 07/2025 and the earlier Nationality Act 07/2022
ST.additional_fees: USD 5,000 submission fee; approximately USD 750 in document fees (USD 250 citizenship certificate, USD 350 passport, USD 150 national ID); contribution is payable only after approval-in-principle, with 90 days to settle (a further 90-day extension can be requested)
ST.processing_time: officially targeted at 1-2.5 months from application to approval, with passport issuance around 3-4 months; however, as of mid-2026, independent trackers report the program experiencing significant delays, with applications now commonly taking 8 months or longer
ST.physical_presence_requirement: none required — fully remote application, no residency, language, or interview requirement
ST.due_diligence: no interview requirement; standard KYC and source-of-funds review conducted by the Citizenship by Investment Unit, operationally supported by STP Service Advisory FZCO (Dubai) under a 10-year exclusive agreement; there is no official .gov website for the program, as all applications are processed through the Dubai-based Citizenship Investment Unit
ST.family_inclusion: spouse; dependent children; parents; grandparents — citizenship extends to future generations of the applicant's descendants under the Citizenship Act
ST.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is granted immediately on approval — no residency period
ST.renewal_requirements: citizenship is permanent, including a national ID card issued alongside the passport
ST.eligibility_criteria: 18+; open to applicants of all nationalities except North Korea; clean criminal record; verifiable source of funds
ST.key_benefits: one of the lowest-cost CBI programs globally; fully remote with no interview; can elect to become a São Tomé tax resident with no capital gains, inheritance, or wealth tax, and personal tax rates of 0-25% with an extensive double-taxation-treaty network
ST.taxation_notes: no personal income tax, capital gains tax, or inheritance tax
ST.application_steps: engage a licensed marketing agent (direct applications to the CIU are not accepted); complete KYC and source-of-funds documentation; receive an approval-in-principle from the government; make the NTF contribution within 90 days of approval (extendable by a further 90 days); name is published in a local gazette; receive citizenship certificate, national ID, and passport
ST.dual_citizenship: Permitted — no requirement to renounce any prior nationality

PT.program_name: Golden Visa (ARI — Autorizacao de Residencia para Investimento)
PT.investment_route: Cultural heritage donation (250000 EUR, or 200000 EUR in low-density areas); Capital transfer into a qualifying investment/venture capital fund (500000 EUR); Job creation (10+ jobs); Direct residential real estate purchase was removed from the program in 2023
PT.investment_breakdown: fund route requires the fund itself to be regulated by the CMVM and not directly or indirectly hold residential real estate; donation route is the lowest-cost entry point
PT.additional_fees: NIF (tax number) registration, legal fees, and AIMA administrative/biometric fees are separate from the core investment, typically several thousand EUR total
PT.processing_time: 12-36 months (application backlog has historically extended timelines beyond official targets)
PT.physical_presence_requirement: 7 days in Portugal in year 1, then 14 days in each subsequent 2-year period — one of the lowest physical presence requirements of any EU golden visa
PT.due_diligence: standard due diligence through AIMA (Portugal's immigration agency, formerly SEF)
PT.family_inclusion: Spouse or partner; Dependent children; Dependent parents of either spouse
PT.naturalization_timeline: Portugal's Nationality Law was amended by Decree 48/XVII, signed 3 May 2026 and in force from 19 May 2026: the general naturalization period was extended from 5 years to 10 years of legal residence for most applicants, and to 7 years for nationals of EU and CPLP (Portuguese-speaking) countries; the residence clock now runs from the date the first residence card is issued rather than the application date; a new A2-level Portuguese language test, a civic/historical knowledge test, and a formal declaration of commitment to democratic principles are also required; citizenship applications formally submitted before 19 May 2026 continue to be assessed under the previous 5-year rule
PT.renewal_requirements: residence permit renewed every 2 years, contingent on maintaining the qualifying investment and minimum presence
PT.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Valid private health insurance; Verifiable source of funds
PT.key_benefits: Access to the Schengen Area for visa-free travel; One of the lowest physical presence requirements among EU programs; Non-habitual resident tax regime available separately for qualifying new tax residents
PT.taxation_notes: non-habitual resident (NHR) regime, where still available to new applicants, offers reduced tax rates on qualifying foreign-source income for a fixed number of years
PT.application_steps: choose investment route; obtain a Portuguese NIF and bank account; submit the AIMA application online; attend biometrics appointment; receive the residence permit and renew every 2 years
PT.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Portugal imposes no restriction on holding multiple nationalities and does not require renunciation of any prior citizenship

GR.investment_route: Real estate purchase at one of three tiers: EUR 250,000 for a commercial-to-residential conversion or listed-building restoration (available anywhere in Greece); EUR 400,000 for standard residential property outside the prime-zone list; EUR 800,000 in Athens, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini, and islands with over 3,100 inhabitants; alternatively, investment in an eligible fund or bank deposit
GR.investment_breakdown: under Circular No.1/2026 (effective 21 April 2026), the qualifying investment must be a single property (the 'Single Property Rule') with a main living space of at least 120 square metres for the EUR 400,000 and EUR 800,000 tiers; auxiliary spaces like storage and parking may count toward total value but not always toward the 120 sqm minimum; funds must originate from outside Greece via a compliant banking channel; legal basis is Law 5038/2023, Law 5007/2022, and Law 5100/2024
GR.additional_fees: AFM (Greek Tax ID) registration required; approximately EUR 2,000 government fee via the e-Paravolo system; property transfer tax around 3%, notary and legal fees separately; since the 2024 reform, short-term rental platforms (Airbnb, Booking.com, and similar) are banned on qualifying properties, with fines of EUR 50,000 per violation — only long-term rentals of 12+ months are permitted
GR.processing_time: approximately 90 days via the Ministry of Migration and Asylum; a Blue Certificate grants immediate temporary stay while the permit is processed
GR.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain the residence permit
GR.due_diligence: standard due diligence tied to the property purchase and source-of-funds verification
GR.family_inclusion: spouse or civil-union partner (full independent rights); unmarried children under 21 (extended to 24 if in full-time education); parents of the main applicant or spouse, under the Family Reunification (O.1) provision
GR.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is separate from the Golden Visa and is not a guaranteed or accelerated outcome of it; naturalization normally requires approximately 7 years of genuine residence in Greece, plus Greek language proficiency and integration/civic knowledge steps — a passive Golden Visa holder who does not actually reside in Greece does not meet this genuine-residence requirement
GR.renewal_requirements: permit is valid for 5 years and renewable indefinitely provided the qualifying investment is maintained
GR.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
GR.key_benefits: No minimum stay requirement makes it popular with investors who don't plan to relocate full time; The purchased property can be rented out for income while the permit remains valid
GR.taxation_notes: non-resident investors are generally taxed only on Greek-source income (including rental income from the qualifying property)
GR.application_steps: select a qualifying property; obtain a Greek tax number (AFM); sign the purchase contract before a notary; register the property; submit the residence permit application with proof of ownership
GR.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Greece allows dual and multiple citizenship

IT.investment_route: Italian government bonds (BTPs), minimum EUR 2,000,000, at least 2 years remaining maturity; Corporate bonds or shares in an Italian limited company, minimum EUR 500,000 (reduced to EUR 250,000 if investing in a registered innovative startup); Public-interest project donation, minimum EUR 1,000,000, in fields such as culture, education, ecology, immigration management, research and development, arts, or heritage; direct residential real estate purchase does not qualify
IT.investment_breakdown: startup investments must go into companies registered on Italy's official innovative-startup register to qualify
IT.additional_fees: no fixed government fee is published on the official portal beyond standard visa and permit-of-stay administrative costs; legal and notary costs apply to the chosen investment structure
IT.processing_time: 2-3 months for the nulla osta clearance, plus consular visa issuance time
IT.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain the residence permit
IT.due_diligence: clean criminal record, proof of financial resources, and a completed investment declaration reviewed by the Investor Visa for Italy Committee (IV4I); the program is currently suspended for non-EU citizens holding dual Russian or Belarusian nationality, per a 2023 Committee order implementing EU Recommendation C(2022) 2028
IT.naturalization_timeline: the Investor Visa does not itself grant citizenship; investors who relocate to Italy may apply for permanent residency after 5 years, or for citizenship through ordinary naturalization after 10 years of legal residence
IT.renewal_requirements: initial residence permit is valid 2 years; renewable once for a further 3 years if the investment is maintained, requiring a new Nulla Osta; if the original investment or donation is maintained for a full 5 years, a long-term (EU) residence card can be requested
IT.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
IT.key_benefits: Access to the Schengen Area; The government's flat-tax regime for new residents (regime forfettario) can substantially reduce tax on foreign-source income
IT.taxation_notes: eligible new residents may opt into a flat annual substitute tax on foreign-sourced income instead of ordinary progressive rates, for a period of up to 15 years
IT.application_steps: register on the investorvisa.mise.gov.it portal and submit application forms, investment selection, and supporting documents; receive a Nulla Osta (certificate of no impediment) from the IV4I Committee within 30 days of a complete submission; apply for the D (entry) visa at an Italian consulate within 6 months of the Nulla Osta and enter Italy within 2 years; apply for the residence permit (permesso di soggiorno) at the local Questura within 8 days of arrival; complete the declared investment within 3 months of arrival and upload proof to the portal for Committee evaluation
IT.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Italy has allowed dual citizenship without requiring renunciation since its 1992 nationality law reform

MT.investment_route: Hold capital assets of at least EUR 500,000 (including at least EUR 150,000 in liquid financial assets), or at least EUR 650,000 (including at least EUR 75,000 in liquid financial assets) — this capital requirement applies to the main applicant only and does not increase with dependants; plus purchase a qualifying property for at least EUR 375,000, or rent one for at least EUR 14,000/year, held 5 years
MT.investment_breakdown: governed by S.L. 217.26 as amended by Legal Notice 146 of 2025; liquid financial assets must be genuine liquid instruments (stocks, bonds, listed shares, funds, bank deposits) — cryptocurrency is explicitly not accepted; since 1 January 2025 the former distinction between South Malta, Gozo, and the rest of Malta for property pricing no longer applies; a 2025 amendment allows switching between owned and rented qualifying property during the compliance period
MT.additional_fees: government administrative fee EUR 60,000 (EUR 15,000 payable within 1 month of submission, remaining EUR 45,000 within 2 months of Approval in Principle); separate government contribution EUR 37,000 (same for purchase or rental route); charitable donation of at least EUR 2,000 to a registered NGO; EUR 7,500 per adult dependant excluding spouse and children under 18; minimum EUR 100,000 health insurance coverage across Malta and Europe per beneficiary; residence card fee EUR 500 per person
MT.processing_time: a complete, well-prepared application commonly reaches a Letter of Approval in Principle within 4-6 months of submission; a Temporary Residence option can place the applicant in Malta within about 2 months while the permanent application is processed
MT.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required; physical presence in Malta is needed only for biometric data capture
MT.due_diligence: applicant must not be a national of, or have close ties to, a sanctioned or RMA-ineligible country; must be fit and proper with a clean criminal record and pose no threat to national security, public policy, public health, or public interest; multi-tier due diligence conducted by the Residency Malta Agency on the applicant and all dependants
MT.family_inclusion: spouse or equivalent partner; children under 18 including adopted children; children 18 and under 29 at time of application if unmarried and principally dependent (no age cap if certified disabled); parents and grandparents of any age who are principally dependent — up to 4 generations can be included in one application
MT.naturalization_timeline: the MPRP grants residence, not citizenship, and does not lead to citizenship as a matter of course; separate Maltese citizenship by naturalisation ordinarily requires long lawful residence assessed case-by-case and is entirely discretionary; a distinct 'citizenship by naturalisation on the basis of merit' route exists under Article 10(9) of the Citizenship Act for exceptional contributions, administered by the Community Malta Agency — this is unrelated to the MPRP and is not a guaranteed pathway
MT.renewal_requirements: the Certificate of Maltese Residence itself is permanent and does not expire; the physical residence card is valid 5 years and renewable; the qualifying property must be held (as owned or rented) for the first 5 years, after which the specific value/rent thresholds fall away but a residential property title must still be maintained together with valid health insurance
MT.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds; Valid health insurance covering Malta
MT.key_benefits: visa-free travel within the Schengen Area for 90 days in any 180-day period; MPRP residence cardholders are exempt from ETIAS authorisation and fall outside EES short-stay registration once the residence card is held; no minimum stay requirement; important: the April 2025 CJEU ruling (Case C-181/23) that struck down Malta's former citizenship-by-investment scheme did NOT affect the MPRP, since the MPRP grants residence rather than nationality and was not the subject of that case
MT.taxation_notes: the MPRP confers no special tax status; ordinary Maltese tax rules apply — a non-domiciled Malta-resident is generally taxed on Maltese-source income and gains, and on foreign income remitted to Malta, but not on unremitted foreign income
MT.application_steps: submit through an RMA Licensed Agent (direct applications are not accepted); pay the EUR 15,000 initial administrative fee within 1 month; undergo Residency Malta Agency due diligence; on approval, receive a Letter of Approval in Principle; within 2 months pay the remaining EUR 45,000 administrative fee; within 8 months of that letter, settle the EUR 37,000 contribution, secure the qualifying property, make the donation, and arrange health insurance; receive the Certificate of Maltese Residence and complete biometrics for the residence card
MT.dual_citizenship: not directly applicable — MPRP grants residence, not citizenship; Malta's separate citizenship law generally permits dual citizenship

CY.investment_route: Purchase of a first-sale house or apartment from a development company (one or two units from the same developer), minimum EUR 300,000 plus VAT; alternatively, investment in commercial real estate, Cyprus company share capital, or units in a Cyprus collective investment fund, same threshold
CY.investment_breakdown: at least EUR 200,000 of the EUR 300,000 must be paid before the application is submitted; legal basis is Regulation 6(2) of the Aliens and Immigration Regulations, with criteria revised effective 2 May 2023; applicants who lodged Sale Agreements between 2 January and 28 April 2023 may still apply under the earlier 24 March 2021 criteria
CY.additional_fees: VAT on the property purchase, legal and translation fees apply separately from the core investment
CY.processing_time: officially around 2 months, though practitioners report 4-8 months in practice
CY.physical_presence_requirement: must visit Cyprus at least once every 2 years to keep the permit valid — this applies to every family member included on the permit, and even a brief visit satisfies the requirement; failure to visit can result in revocation
CY.due_diligence: clean criminal record and general suitability required; applicant and spouse must sign a declaration confirming they do not intend to take up employment in Cyprus (the sole exception being an unpaid director role in the invested company); from 1 September 2026, applicants and dependants must also submit blood test results for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV and syphilis, plus a chest X-ray for tuberculosis
CY.family_inclusion: spouse; dependent children under 18; children studying in Cyprus may hold a temporary student permit and apply for their own Permanent Residency (with a further fee) once they complete their studies, regardless of age
CY.naturalization_timeline: the CBI citizenship route linked to this permanent residence scheme was suspended in 2020; PRP holders may apply for citizenship through ordinary naturalization after 8 years of residence (7 years within the preceding 10, plus a final continuous 12 months)
CY.renewal_requirements: the Permanent Residence Permit is a lifetime permit with no renewal requirement, subject to the once-every-2-years visit condition
CY.eligibility_criteria: secured annual income of at least EUR 50,000 for the main applicant, plus EUR 15,000 for a spouse and EUR 10,000 per dependent minor child; income may come from salary, pension, dividends, bank interest, or rent; for the property route, income must originate from abroad; clean criminal record
CY.key_benefits: fast processing relative to most EU programs; minimal physical presence requirement (a single visit every 2 years); Cyprus is actively progressing toward Schengen accession, often referenced around 2026, which if completed would meaningfully increase the mobility value of this permit
CY.taxation_notes: Cyprus's non-domicile regime exempts qualifying residents from tax on foreign dividends and interest for 17 years
CY.application_steps: purchase a qualifying new-build property; submit the residence permit application with proof of income and property ownership; attend interview if required; permit issued
CY.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Cyprus allows dual and multiple citizenship (note: this specific Permanent Residence Permit does not itself grant citizenship)

HU.investment_route: Investment certificates worth at least EUR 250,000 issued by a real estate fund registered with the Hungarian National Bank and on the Constitution Protection Office's approved list, with at least 40% of the fund's assets in Hungarian residential real estate; or a non-refundable donation of EUR 1,000,000 to a public-interest trust foundation supporting higher education, research, or the arts — the direct EUR 500,000 residential real estate purchase option that existed at launch was removed entirely on 15 January 2025 and is no longer available
HU.investment_breakdown: the fund's investment certificate must have a minimum 5-year maturity and be maintained without withdrawal; the investment must be completed within 93 calendar days of first entry into Hungary on the Guest Investor Visa
HU.additional_fees: 4% property transfer tax on the underlying real estate calculated at market value; 15% personal income tax applies if rental income is generated from the fund's underlying property or from directly acquired eligible property
HU.processing_time: typically 4-6 months; a Guest Investor Visa (D visa) is issued first, following a due diligence check by the Migration Office
HU.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain the permit; holders are not considered Hungarian tax residents if they spend fewer than 183 days in Hungary in any 12-month period
HU.due_diligence: due diligence check conducted by the Migration Office before the Guest Investor Visa is issued, prior to the investment being made
HU.naturalization_timeline: the program does not itself lead to citizenship; after 8 years of residence, holders may apply for citizenship through Hungary's separate ordinary naturalization process
HU.renewal_requirements: the guest investor residence permit is a temporary (not permanent) status, valid for 10 years and renewable for a further 10 years
HU.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
HU.key_benefits: access to the Schengen Area (90 days in any 180); low cost of living relative to Western Europe; universal healthcare access; relaunched July 2024 after the prior bond-based program ended in 2017
HU.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed only if tax-resident in Hungary
HU.application_steps: choose the investment route; submit application to the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing; complete due diligence; residence permit issued
HU.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Hungary allows dual and multiple citizenship (note: this residence program does not itself grant citizenship)

LV.investment_route: real estate purchase (250000 EUR minimum, one or more properties) plus a one-time state fee of approximately 5% of the property value
LV.investment_breakdown: alternative routes include subordinated deposits in a Latvian bank (280000 EUR) or investment in a Latvian company's share capital (50000 EUR plus 40000 EUR paid in state and municipal taxes over 3 years)
LV.additional_fees: notary, legal, and property registration fees apply on top of the purchase price and state fee
LV.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain the residence permit
LV.due_diligence: standard due diligence through the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs
LV.naturalization_timeline: the program does not itself lead to citizenship; a separate ordinary naturalization route applies based on years of residence and a Latvian language test
LV.renewal_requirements: residence permit valid for 5 years initially, renewable subject to continued property ownership
LV.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
LV.key_benefits: Access to the Schengen Area; One of the lower property-investment thresholds among EU golden visa programs
LV.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed only if tax-resident in Latvia
LV.application_steps: select a qualifying property; pay the purchase price and state fee; submit application to the Office of Citizenship and Migration Affairs; residence permit issued
LV.dual_citizenship: Restricted — Latvia only permits dual citizenship with a specific list of countries (mainly EU/EEA/NATO/EFTA states and a small number of others); dual citizenship with most other countries requires special exemption (note: this residence program does not itself grant citizenship)

US.investment_route: Investment in a Targeted Employment Area (TEA — rural or high-unemployment area, 800000 USD) or standard investment elsewhere (1050000 USD); Investment must create or preserve at least 10 full-time US jobs for qualifying workers
US.investment_breakdown: most applicants invest through a USCIS-designated Regional Center, pooling capital into a project rather than directly running a business
US.additional_fees: USCIS filing fees for Form I-526E and Form I-829 (several thousand USD each), plus regional center administrative fees which vary by project
US.processing_time: 18-24 months for I-526E processing, plus additional time for visa/adjustment of status; total timeline can extend well beyond 2 years depending on backlog and country of origin
US.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum physical presence required to maintain conditional status, though standard green card rules on maintaining US residence apply once issued
US.due_diligence: extensive lawful-source-of-funds due diligence — considered among the strictest of any residency-by-investment program globally
US.naturalization_timeline: eligible to apply for US citizenship after 5 years as a lawful permanent resident, the same timeline as any other green card holder
US.renewal_requirements: conditional green card issued for 2 years; Form I-829 must be filed before expiry to remove conditions and receive a standard 10-year green card
US.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable lawful source of investment funds; Investment must create/preserve 10 qualifying US jobs
US.key_benefits: a direct path to a US green card and eventual citizenship with no employer sponsorship or job offer required, unlike most other US work-based visas
US.taxation_notes: US tax residents (including green card holders) are taxed on worldwide income once the green card is issued
US.application_steps: select a Regional Center project or direct investment; file Form I-526E petition with USCIS; obtain conditional green card via consular processing or adjustment of status; file Form I-829 after 2 years to remove conditions
US.dual_citizenship: Permitted in practice — the US naturalization oath contains renunciatory language but the US does not actively enforce it or require proof that another nationality was relinquished, so most naturalized US citizens retain their original citizenship if their home country also allows it

PA.investment_route: Real estate purchase (300000 USD); Securities investment through a licensed Panamanian brokerage (300000 USD, 5yr hold); Fixed-term bank deposit (750000 USD, 5yr hold)
PA.investment_breakdown: real estate route is the most commonly used and can include one or more properties combined to reach the threshold
PA.additional_fees: government and legal processing fees apply in addition to the qualifying investment
PA.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain residency
PA.due_diligence: standard due diligence through Panama's National Immigration Service
PA.naturalization_timeline: eligible to apply for citizenship after 5 years of holding permanent residence, subject to a Spanish-language and civics test
PA.renewal_requirements: permanent residence is granted directly (not a renewable temporary status) provided the qualifying investment is maintained for its hold period
PA.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
PA.key_benefits: One of the fastest routes to permanent (not temporary) residency of any program worldwide; Panama's territorial tax system means foreign-sourced income is not taxed
PA.taxation_notes: territorial tax system — only Panama-sourced income is taxed; foreign-sourced income, including from investments held abroad, is not taxed
PA.application_steps: select the investment route; submit application to the National Immigration Service with proof of investment; complete due diligence; permanent residence card issued
PA.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Panama allows dual and multiple citizenship

SG.investment_route: Business expansion investment in an existing Singapore-based business (10000000 SGD, minimum 3-year track record and revenue thresholds); Investment into a GIP-approved fund (10000000 SGD); Establishment of a new single family office (200000000 SGD assets under management)
SG.investment_breakdown: applicants must submit a detailed business or investment plan for evaluation by the Economic Development Board before any capital is committed
SG.additional_fees: no fixed government fee is published; costs are dominated by the qualifying investment itself and professional advisory fees
SG.processing_time: 6-12 months, including an in-person interview and business plan evaluation
SG.physical_presence_requirement: case-by-case, generally expected to demonstrate genuine commitment to Singapore over time
SG.due_diligence: extensive due diligence including business track record, net worth verification, and a formal interview; among the most selective residency-by-investment programs globally, with a high rejection rate
SG.naturalization_timeline: the GIP does not itself grant citizenship; separate naturalization is possible after an extended period of residence and is highly selective
SG.renewal_requirements: permanent residence is granted directly if approved, without an intermediate temporary-visa stage
SG.eligibility_criteria: A proven entrepreneurial or business track record; Substantial verifiable net worth well beyond the headline investment figure
SG.key_benefits: Access to Singapore's status as a leading Asia-Pacific financial and business hub; Permanent residency (not merely a long-stay visa) if approved
SG.taxation_notes: Singapore taxes residents only on Singapore-sourced income and on foreign income remitted into Singapore; foreign income kept offshore is generally not taxed
SG.application_steps: submit a business or investment proposal to the Economic Development Board; undergo evaluation and interview; receive approval in principle; complete the investment; permanent residence granted
SG.dual_citizenship: Not permitted — Singapore requires renunciation of all other citizenships upon naturalization (note: this program grants permanent residence, not citizenship, but Singapore's broader citizenship law is relevant for investors planning that far ahead)

BR.investment_route: Business investment (500000 BRL standard, reduced to 150000 BRL for approved technology, AI, or green-energy startups); Passive real estate purchase (1000000 BRL in urban centers, 700000 BRL in the North/Northeast)
BR.investment_breakdown: the reduced startup threshold applies only to companies registered with Brazil's approved innovation programs
BR.additional_fees: company registration and legal fees apply in addition to the core investment for the business route
BR.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain the residence permit
BR.due_diligence: standard due diligence tied to the registered investment plan
BR.naturalization_timeline: eligible to apply for permanent residency after 4 years, and for citizenship after a further 4 years of permanent residence (8 years total)
BR.renewal_requirements: residence permit renewed periodically provided the investment is maintained
BR.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds; Registered investment plan filed with Brazilian authorities
BR.key_benefits: One of the lowest-cost investor residency routes among major economies; A Brazilian passport grants residency rights across the 9-country Mercosur bloc (Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay)
BR.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed only if tax-resident in Brazil (183+ days per year)
BR.application_steps: register the investment plan with the relevant Brazilian agency; apply for the visa at a Brazilian consulate or convert status in-country; residence permit issued
BR.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Brazil allows dual and multiple citizenship

NZ.investment_route: Growth category (5000000 NZD into managed funds, direct investment, or bonds, with at least 50% in growth/higher-risk assets, minimum stay 21 days over 3 years); Balanced category (10000000 NZD, at least 25% in growth assets, minimum stay 105 days over 5 years)
NZ.investment_breakdown: acceptable growth assets include New Zealand equities, private equity, and venture capital; philanthropic donations can offset up to a portion of the required minimum stay
NZ.additional_fees: visa application fees and approved financial adviser costs apply in addition to the qualifying investment
NZ.processing_time: 4-6 months for visa approval, plus the investment period itself before permanent residence is granted
NZ.physical_presence_requirement: 21 days over 3 years (Growth category) or 105 days over 5 years (Balanced category)
NZ.due_diligence: standard due diligence plus verification of business/investment experience and English language ability
NZ.naturalization_timeline: leads to permanent residence at the end of the qualifying investment period, with citizenship available afterward through New Zealand's standard residence-based naturalization route
NZ.renewal_requirements: the resident visa converts to permanent residence once the investment period and presence requirements are met
NZ.eligibility_criteria: Proven business or investment experience; Verifiable source of funds; English language ability (or a fee to waive the requirement for dependants)
NZ.key_benefits: Relaunched in 2025 with lower thresholds and shorter minimum-stay requirements than the prior program; Strong rule of law, low corruption, and high quality of life
NZ.taxation_notes: worldwide income taxed if tax-resident in New Zealand; New Zealand does not levy a general capital gains tax on most personal investments
NZ.application_steps: submit an Expression of Interest; obtain approval in principle; make the qualifying investment within 12 months; visa granted; meet minimum stay requirement over the investment period
NZ.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — New Zealand allows dual and multiple citizenship

PY.investment_route: Investment in an approved tourism-sector project (hospitality, eco-tourism, or related infrastructure)
PY.investment_breakdown: qualifying projects are pre-vetted and listed by Paraguay's Ministry of Industry and Commerce
PY.additional_fees: government processing fees apply in addition to the qualifying investment
PY.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum stay required to maintain residency
PY.due_diligence: standard due diligence through the Ministry of Industry and Commerce and immigration authorities
PY.naturalization_timeline: eligible to apply for citizenship after 3 years of permanent residence, one of the shortest naturalization timelines among residency-by-investment programs
PY.renewal_requirements: permanent residence is granted directly and does not require periodic renewal in the way temporary visas do
PY.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable source of funds
PY.key_benefits: One of the lowest entry thresholds and fastest South American residency-by-investment routes; Paraguay's territorial tax system means foreign-sourced income is untaxed
PY.taxation_notes: territorial tax system — only Paraguay-sourced income is taxed
PY.application_steps: select a qualifying tourism project; submit application to the Ministry of Industry and Commerce; complete due diligence; permanent residence granted
PY.dual_citizenship: Fully permitted — Paraguay allows dual and multiple citizenship

MC.investment_route: bank deposit of at least 500000 EUR with a Monaco-based bank, combined with securing accommodation in Monaco (purchase or lease) and demonstrating financial self-sufficiency
MC.investment_breakdown: the deposit is not a donation — funds remain the applicant's own assets and can typically be invested through the same bank once residency is secured
MC.additional_fees: bank account setup costs, accommodation costs (purchase or lease, which can be substantial given Monaco's property market), and application processing fees apply on top of the deposit
MC.physical_presence_requirement: must genuinely reside in Monaco; the residence card requires periodic renewal that depends on demonstrating actual presence
MC.due_diligence: standard due diligence through the Monaco government and the sponsoring bank
MC.family_inclusion: spouse and dependent children can apply for residence cards alongside the main applicant
MC.naturalization_timeline: eligible to apply for Monegasque naturalization after 10 years of residence, one of the longer timelines among wealth-based residency programs, and naturalization remains fully discretionary
MC.renewal_requirements: the initial residence card is valid for 1 year, then renewable for 3-year periods, contingent on continued residence and financial self-sufficiency
MC.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Demonstrated financial self-sufficiency; No employment income earned outside Monaco required (though many residents do work)
MC.key_benefits: Monaco levies no personal income tax on residents (French nationals are a historic exception under a bilateral treaty); Access to one of the world's most secure and prestigious residency addresses
MC.taxation_notes: no personal income tax for non-French residents; no capital gains tax on personal investments
MC.application_steps: open a qualifying account with a Monaco bank and deposit the required funds; secure accommodation; submit residence application with proof of funds and accommodation; attend interview; residence card issued
MC.dual_citizenship: Not applicable to this residence permit; Monegasque naturalization, when eventually pursued, generally requires renunciation of prior nationality

AD.investment_route: Investment in Andorran real estate, company shares, government debt; Financial instruments (400000 EUR), plus a mandatory 50000 EUR interest-free deposit with the Andorran Financial Authority (AFA), refunded when residence status ends
AD.investment_breakdown: the AFA deposit is separate from and additional to the 400000 EUR qualifying investment, and is returned in full if the applicant later relinquishes residency
AD.additional_fees: legal and notary fees for the property or investment purchase apply on top of the investment and deposit amounts
AD.physical_presence_requirement: minimum 90 days per year physical presence required to maintain the permit
AD.due_diligence: standard due diligence through the Andorran immigration department
AD.family_inclusion: spouse and dependent children can be included as dependants on the same application
AD.naturalization_timeline: citizenship is available after 20 years of residence, one of the longest naturalization timelines of any residency-by-investment program, and requires renunciation of the applicant's existing nationality since Andorra does not generally permit dual citizenship for naturalized citizens
AD.renewal_requirements: residence permit is renewable periodically provided the 90-day presence requirement and investment are maintained
AD.eligibility_criteria: 18+; Clean criminal record; Verifiable annual income of at least approximately 54900 EUR (rising with each dependant); Private health insurance
AD.key_benefits: Andorra's low-tax regime (income tax capped around 10%) combined with a high quality of life in the Pyrenees; The AFA deposit is fully refundable, unlike a donation-based program
AD.taxation_notes: personal income tax capped at approximately 10%; no wealth tax and no inheritance tax
AD.application_steps: select the qualifying investment; open the mandatory AFA deposit account; submit residence application with proof of income and health insurance; attend interview; permit issued
AD.dual_citizenship: Not applicable to this residence permit; Andorran naturalization, when eventually pursued after 20 years, generally requires renunciation of prior nationality since Andorra does not recognize dual citizenship for the naturalized

MY.investment_route: Fixed deposit in a Malaysian bank, tiered by program level: Silver (150000 USD), Gold (500000 USD), Platinum (1000000 USD), plus a mandatory property purchase at each tier (Silver 600000 MYR, Gold 1000000 MYR, Platinum 2000000 MYR); A lower-cost Special Economic Zone route exists at 65000 USD (under 50) or 32000 USD (50 and older)
MY.investment_breakdown: up to 50% of the fixed deposit can be withdrawn after the first year for an approved local property purchase, medical expenses, or education once conditions are met; the purchased property must be held for 10 years
MY.additional_fees: licensed operator/agent fees typically run 20000-50000 MYR on top of the deposit and property costs
MY.processing_time: several months, varying by tier and completeness of documentation
MY.physical_presence_requirement: minimum 60 days per year physical presence required to maintain most tiers
MY.due_diligence: standard due diligence including a Letter of Good Conduct from the applicant's home country
MY.family_inclusion: Spouse; Dependent children; — under specific conditions — dependent parents
MY.naturalization_timeline: MM2H is a residency pass only and does not itself lead to permanent residency or citizenship
MY.renewal_requirements: visa validity ranges from 5 years (Silver) to 20 years (Platinum), renewable subject to maintaining the fixed deposit and property conditions
MY.eligibility_criteria: Minimum age 21 (Silver/SEZ) or 25 (Gold/Platinum); Clean criminal record; Valid medical insurance (waived for applicants over 59)
MY.key_benefits: Foreign income and funds remitted under the program, plus interest earned on the required fixed deposit, are not taxed; Access to Malaysia's healthcare and international schools; Only the Platinum tier carries limited work rights
MY.taxation_notes: foreign-sourced income and remitted funds under MM2H are not taxed; interest on the fixed deposit itself is also tax-exempt
MY.application_steps: select a tier; open the fixed deposit account; complete the mandatory property purchase; submit application with financial and medical documents to MOTAC; visa issued
MY.dual_citizenship: Not applicable — MM2H is a residency pass only and does not lead to citizenship; Malaysia does not generally recognize dual citizenship for its own nationals

TH.program_name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Visa — Wealthy Global Citizen category
TH.investment_route: Minimum 1000000 USD in global assets, including at least 500000 USD invested in Thai government bonds, foreign direct investment; Thai real estate; Alternative categories exist for remote workers and pensioners with lower financial thresholds
TH.investment_breakdown: the Wealthy Global Citizen category has no age requirement, unlike the Wealthy Pensioner category which requires applicants to be 50 or older with qualifying passive income
TH.additional_fees: government fee of 50000 THB (approximately 1400 USD) covers the full 10-year visa, not charged annually
TH.processing_time: typically 4-8 weeks after a complete application is submitted to the Board of Investment (BOI)
TH.physical_presence_requirement: no minimum annual stay required to maintain the visa, though annual reporting to immigration is mandatory
TH.due_diligence: standard due diligence through Thailand's Board of Investment in cooperation with the Immigration Bureau
TH.family_inclusion: spouse and dependent children can be included on the same application
TH.naturalization_timeline: the LTR visa does not lead to permanent residence or citizenship; it is a long-stay visa route only
TH.renewal_requirements: issued as a 10-year visa structured as two 5-year stamps; the second 5 years requires re-confirming eligibility, it is not automatic
TH.eligibility_criteria: Minimum health insurance coverage of 50000 USD; Or a minimum balance of 100000 USD in a savings account as alternative financial security
TH.key_benefits: One of the longest-duration Asia-Pacific residency visas without requiring permanent relocation; Includes streamlined digital work permit access and tax benefits for eligible categories; Annual reporting only, not the 90-day reporting required of other Thai visas
TH.taxation_notes: LTR visa holders under the Wealthy Global Citizen and other qualifying categories may access preferential personal income tax treatment on foreign-sourced income under Thai Revenue Department rules
